meta.question: Q-01: the user asked to rank hotels by Michelin restaurants within 1 hour by subway or bus.
meta.answer: Las Vegas has no subway or metro rail. The 'by subway or bus' constraint is therefore modelled on three systems that do not share a ticket: RTC transit buses (The Deuce / SDX / local routes), the Las Vegas Monorail, and the Boring Company Vegas Loop.
meta.honesty: Every minute figure here is an ESTIMATE built from official station lists and route maps, rounded to 5 minutes. No official source publishes door-to-door travel times. These are planning estimates, not timetables.
meta.generated_by: scripts/build.py recomputes michelin_within_60 and michelin_within_20 in data/hotels.json from this matrix — do not hand-edit those two fields.
meta.route_203_correction: An earlier version of this matrix recorded Chinatown / Spring Mountain Rd as reachable only by car or rideshare, with no RTC service. That was wrong. Route 203 runs the length of Spring Mountain Road and its official timetable carries a timed stop at Las Vegas Blvd. Weekday runs take about 10 to 17 minutes from Decatur to Las Vegas Blvd depending on the time of day (14 minutes is used as the midpoint). Because the Chinatown zone holds seven of the 24 MICHELIN listings, the correction raises the north Strip's short-trip counts and makes Wynn/Resorts World/SAHARA the best bases for that cluster. Timetable: https://rtcws.rtcsnv.com/routePDF/203.pdf
meta.published_rule: The minutes matrix and model counts are historical unvalidated research; excluded from public verified rankings. See field-level evidence and blank bus-count cells in data/verification.json. The Monorail/Loop are optional non-bus modes, not substitutes for proof of bus journeys.

systems.name: Las Vegas Monorail
systems.fare_note: $6.25 paper / $5.75 electronic single; 7-day $64 / $59.95 per person. Nevada-resident $1 local fare requires valid ID and has purchase restrictions; not a visitor fare. See official ticket page for other durations.
systems.note: 3.9 miles end to end, roughly 4–8 minute headways. Does NOT reach the airport or downtown.

systems.name: RTC Transit — The Deuce & SDX
systems.fare_note: Strip & Downtown Express / Deuce: $4 single, $6 2-hour, $8 24-hour, $20 3-day (regular fare; reduced fare $2/$3/$4/$10). Residential routes: $2 single regular / $1 reduced, $3 2-hour, $5 24-hour, $20 7-day. Source: https://www.rtcsnv.com/ways-to-travel/fares-passes/ (fetched 27 Nov 2026).
systems.note: The only 24-hour option, and the only one that reaches downtown (Fremont Street) and the Arts District.

systems.name: RTC Route 203 — Spring Mountain / Desert Inn / Lamb
systems.fare_note: Covered by any RTC Strip & All Access or residential pass: $4 single, $6 two-hour, $8 24-hour, $20 three-day. Passes are valid on all routes.
systems.hours: Runs seven days a week from early morning until late evening. Check the timetable for the exact first and last trip.
systems.verification: VERIFIED. Unlike every other figure in this matrix, this route has a published timetable with timed stops, so the travel time below is read off the operator's own schedule rather than estimated.
systems.published_timing: The timetable runs sampled give Decatur to Las Vegas Blvd. about 8 to 17 minutes depending on direction, day and time (weekday eastbound 10–17; Saturday westbound 8–9; 14 minutes is the model midpoint), with Rainbow in between. That is the whole Spring Mountain Road corridor the Chinatown restaurants sit on. Combined with a walk to the stop and a platform wait, the north Strip lands at about 34 minutes door to door.
systems.why_it_matters: This is the ONLY published travel time in the model, and it is the one that decides whether the seven Chinatown restaurants are inside the one-hour limit. They are: from the north end of the Strip, where Spring Mountain Road crosses Las Vegas Boulevard, Route 203 puts Chinatown about 30 minutes away door to door.
systems.scope_note: Route 203 stops at Las Vegas Blvd at the north end of the Strip, near Wynn, Encore, Resorts World and SAHARA. It does not reach the center or south Strip, so those hotels need a northbound leg first.
systems.note: RTC local route, not an express. Runs the full length of Spring Mountain Road, which is the road the Chinatown MICHELIN cluster sits on. Stops about every quarter mile.

systems.name: Vegas Loop (Boring Company)
systems.fare_note: Operator examples: LVCC to Strip $5; LVCC to Thomas & Mack $8. Other trip fares are not verified; check operator ticketing. Loop is not an RTC bus or subway.
systems.note: Point-to-point in Tesla vehicles, not a rail line. Fare bands vary by station pair.

finding.inside_60: The Strip is about 4 miles long and Chinatown is about 3 miles west of it, so EVERY hotel in the dataset — including Henderson and Summerlin — reaches all 24 Michelin listings inside 60 minutes. The user's literal metric returns a flat 24/24 for every property and therefore cannot rank anything.
finding.fix: A second, stricter column was added: how many Michelin restaurants are within a 20-MINUTE one-way trip. That column separates the field and drives the ranking.
finding.disclose: This substitution is a material interpretation of the brief and is raised as Q-01 on the Questions page.
finding.route_203_note: Correction applied: the north Strip to Chinatown timing is 34 minutes, not the 20 previously estimated. It is built from Route 203's timetable (about 8 to 17 minutes Decatur to Las Vegas Blvd; the model uses 14, the midpoint) plus a 7-minute walk from Wynn to the Spring Mountain Road stop, an 8-minute platform wait and a 5-minute walk at the far end. Anchored at Wynn, the north Strip hotel closest to that junction; Venetian and Palazzo sit further south and will take longer.
